s: Last summer, my family tried something unusual: we swapped homes with a family from Portugal for three weeks.
We found them on a website that is used by thousands of families.
paragraphs.zh: 去年夏天，我們家試了一件不尋常的事：和一個葡萄牙家庭交換房子住了三個星期。我們是在一個有數千個家庭使用的網站上找到他們的。

s: Before they arrived, my mother was worried that they would break something.
She hid our best plates and wrote a long list of rules.
paragraphs.zh: 他們來之前，我媽媽擔心他們會打破東西。她把最好的盤子藏了起來，還寫了一長串規則。

s: Their house, which was near the sea, was smaller than ours but full of light.
They had left us fresh bread, local cheese and a map with their favorite beaches.
paragraphs.zh: 他們的房子靠近海邊，比我們家小，但充滿陽光。他們給我們留了新鮮的麵包、當地的起司，還有一張標著他們最愛海灘的地圖。

s: When we got home, everything was cleaner than before.
My mother admitted that her list had been unnecessary.
We are already planning our next swap.
paragraphs.zh: 我們回到家時，一切都比原來還乾淨。媽媽承認她那張清單根本沒必要。我們已經在計畫下一次交換了。

s: Until two years ago, Daniel was working as an accountant in a large bank.
He earned a good salary, but he felt bored every single day.
paragraphs.zh: 直到兩年前，丹尼爾都在一家大銀行當會計師。他薪水很好，卻每天都覺得無聊。

s: His real passion had always been cooking.
At weekends he used to make tacos for his friends, who kept telling him to open a restaurant.
paragraphs.zh: 他真正熱愛的一直是做菜。以前週末他常做墨西哥捲餅給朋友吃，朋友們一直叫他開餐廳。

s: A restaurant was too expensive, so he bought an old truck instead and repaired it himself.
Now he parks it outside office buildings at lunchtime.
paragraphs.zh: 開餐廳太貴了，所以他改買了一輛舊卡車，自己修好。現在他午餐時間就把車停在辦公大樓外面。

s: He works longer hours than before and earns less money.
However, he says he has never been happier.
"If I had stayed at the bank," he says, "I would still be dreaming."
paragraphs.zh: 他現在工作時間比以前長，賺的錢也比較少。不過他說他從來沒有這麼快樂過。「如果我當初留在銀行，」他說，「我到現在還只是在做夢。」

s: I had always wanted to travel by night train, so last autumn I booked a sleeper from Vienna to Rome.
The journey took fourteen hours.
paragraphs.zh: 我一直想搭夜車旅行，所以去年秋天訂了從維也納到羅馬的臥鋪。整趟旅程花了十四個小時。

s: My compartment was tiny, and I was sharing it with two strangers.
One was a retired teacher from Canada, and the other was a student who was studying art in Florence.
paragraphs.zh: 我的包廂很小，和兩個陌生人共用。一位是加拿大來的退休老師，另一位是在佛羅倫斯念藝術的學生。

s: While the train was crossing the mountains, we shared snacks and stories.
I didn't sleep much because of the noise, but I didn't mind.
paragraphs.zh: 火車穿越山區的時候，我們分享零食，也聊了很多故事。因為噪音，我沒怎麼睡，但我不在意。

s: When I woke up, the sun was rising over Italian hills.
A flight would have been faster, of course.
But I would never have met two such interesting people.
paragraphs.zh: 我醒來時，太陽正從義大利的山丘升起。當然，搭飛機會快得多。可是那樣我就永遠不會遇到這麼有趣的兩個人了。

s: Last July, our town experienced the worst heatwave ever recorded.
For ten days, temperatures stayed above forty degrees.
paragraphs.zh: 去年七月，我們鎮上經歷了有紀錄以來最嚴重的熱浪。連續十天，氣溫都在四十度以上。

s: Many old people were told to stay indoors during the afternoon.
The town hall was turned into a cool room where anyone could rest for free.
paragraphs.zh: 許多老年人被告知下午要待在室內。鎮公所被改成了避暑室，任何人都可以免費在那裡休息。

s: I was working at a café at the time.
We sold more ice cream in one week than in the whole of the previous summer.
But the heat in the kitchen was almost unbearable.
paragraphs.zh: 那時我在一家咖啡館打工。我們一週賣出的冰淇淋，比前一年整個夏天還多。可是廚房裡熱得幾乎受不了。

s: Scientists say that heatwaves like this will become more common.
Our town has since planted hundreds of trees to give more shade.
paragraphs.zh: 科學家說，這樣的熱浪會越來越常見。從那以後，我們鎮上種了好幾百棵樹，好提供更多遮蔭。

s: When my toaster stopped working, I was going to throw it away and buy a new one.
Then a neighbor told me about the repair café in our local library.
paragraphs.zh: 我的烤麵包機壞掉時，我原本打算丟掉再買一台新的。後來鄰居跟我說，我們這區的圖書館有一家修理咖啡館。

s: It is open on the first Saturday of every month.
Volunteers, who are often retired engineers, fix broken things for free.
You only pay for new parts.
paragraphs.zh: 它每個月第一個星期六開放。志工們多半是退休的工程師，免費幫人修理壞掉的東西。你只要付新零件的錢。

s: While I was waiting, I drank coffee and watched a woman repair a lamp.
A man next to me was having his bike fixed.
paragraphs.zh: 等的時候，我喝著咖啡，看一位女士修檯燈。我旁邊的男士正在請人修他的腳踏車。

s: My toaster only needed a new wire, which cost two dollars.
I have been going there ever since, and I have learned to fix small things myself.
paragraphs.zh: 我的烤麵包機只需要換一條兩塊錢的電線。從那以後我就一直去，還學會了自己修些小東西。

s: When I was sixteen, I spent a year as an exchange student in a small town in Japan.
I had been studying Japanese for only six months.
paragraphs.zh: 我十六歲時，在日本一個小鎮當了一年交換學生。那時我才學了六個月的日文。

s: The first weeks were hard.
I couldn't understand the lessons, and I was too shy to speak.
I often ate lunch alone and felt homesick.
paragraphs.zh: 頭幾個星期很辛苦。我聽不懂課，又太害羞不敢開口。我常常一個人吃午餐，很想家。

s: Things changed when I joined the school's volleyball club.
The training was tough, but my teammates were patient and taught me lots of everyday words.
paragraphs.zh: 我加入學校的排球社後，情況才有了改變。訓練很辛苦，但隊友們很有耐心，教了我很多日常用語。

s: By the end of the year, I could chat easily with my host family.
If I hadn't joined the club, I would probably have gone home early.
paragraphs.zh: 到了年底，我已經可以輕鬆地和寄宿家庭聊天。如果我當初沒有加入社團，大概早就回家了。

s: In our city, the last bus used to leave the center at eleven o'clock.
Young people who worked late or went out often had to pay for expensive taxis.
paragraphs.zh: 在我們市裡，末班公車以前十一點就從市中心開走了。晚下班或出去玩的年輕人常常得花大錢坐計程車。

s: Last year a group of students started a campaign for night buses.
They collected over five thousand signatures and presented them to the city council.
paragraphs.zh: 去年，一群學生發起了爭取夜間公車的運動。他們收集了五千多個連署，交給了市議會。

s: At first the council said the idea was too expensive.
However, the students showed that many restaurant and hospital workers also needed transport at night.
paragraphs.zh: 起初市議會說這個想法太花錢。不過學生們指出，很多餐廳和醫院的員工晚上也需要交通工具。

s: Since March, two night lines have been running on Fridays and Saturdays.
If they are used enough, they will run every night from next year.
paragraphs.zh: 從三月起，兩條夜間路線在星期五和星期六行駛。如果搭的人夠多，明年起就會每晚行駛。

s: I work in an office, and I used to sit for about ten hours a day.
Recently I had been getting pains in my back and neck.
paragraphs.zh: 我在辦公室上班，以前一天大約要坐十個小時。最近我的背和脖子一直在痛。

s: My doctor explained that sitting for long periods is bad for your health, even if you exercise.
She suggested that I should stand up and move every thirty minutes.
paragraphs.zh: 醫生解釋說，就算有運動，長時間坐著也對健康不好。她建議我每三十分鐘站起來動一動。

s: So my company gave me a desk that can be raised or lowered.
Now I stand for part of the morning and take short walks during phone calls.
paragraphs.zh: 於是公司給了我一張可以升降的桌子。現在我早上有一段時間站著工作，講電話時也會短暫走動。

s: After two months, the pain has mostly gone.
Several colleagues have asked for the same desk, and our boss is thinking of buying them for everyone.
paragraphs.zh: 兩個月後，疼痛大多消失了。好幾位同事也要了同樣的桌子，老闆正在考慮幫每個人都買一張。

items.text:
When Rosa Martinez moved into a flat in the centre of town three years ago, she missed one thing more than anything else: her parents' garden. 'I grew up picking tomatoes and beans every summer,' she says. 'Suddenly I had nothing but a tiny balcony.'
Behind her building was an empty piece of land that had been a car park until the company that owned it closed. Rosa wrote to the town council to ask if local people could use it to grow vegetables. 'I didn't expect an answer,' she admits. 'But a month later they said yes — as long as we kept it tidy and didn't build anything permanent.'
The first spring was hard work. Rosa and a few neighbours spent every weekend removing stones and bringing in soil. 'Some people thought we were crazy,' she laughs. 'But when the first lettuces came up, more and more people wanted to join.' Today the garden has forty members, from schoolchildren to pensioners, and each family looks after its own small area.
The garden has changed the street in ways Rosa never imagined. 'People who had lived next to each other for years had never spoken,' she says. 'Now they share seeds, swap recipes and water each other's plants when someone is on holiday.' Last summer the members held their first harvest party, cooking meals with everything they had grown.
Rosa's next plan is to build a small greenhouse so that the garden can be used in winter too. 'We'll need to raise some money first,' she says, 'but after everything we've done, I'm sure we'll find a way.'

tr.zh:
三年前蘿莎·馬丁尼茲搬進市中心的公寓時，最想念的就是爸媽家的菜園。「我從小每年夏天都摘番茄、摘豆子，」她說，「突然間只剩一個小陽台。」
她住的大樓後面有一塊空地，原本是停車場，後來擁有它的公司倒了。蘿莎寫信給市議會，問附近居民能不能用來種菜。「我沒想到會有回音，」她承認，「但一個月後他們答應了，只要我們保持整潔、不蓋永久的建築。」
第一個春天很辛苦。蘿莎和幾個鄰居每個週末都在搬石頭、運土。「有人覺得我們瘋了，」她笑著說，「可是第一批萵苣長出來以後，越來越多人想加入。」現在菜園有四十位成員，從小學生到退休老人都有，每家照顧自己的一小塊地。
菜園帶給這條街的改變是蘿莎沒想到的。「有些人當了好多年鄰居，從來沒說過話，」她說，「現在大家分享種子、交換食譜，有人去度假時還會幫忙澆水。」去年夏天，成員們辦了第一次豐收派對，用自己種的東西做菜。
蘿莎下一步打算蓋一間小溫室，讓菜園冬天也能用。「我們得先籌點錢，」她說，「不過我們都走到這一步了，我相信一定有辦法。」

Learning to swim at forty
I never learnt to swim as a child. My family lived far from the sea, and our town had no pool. (16) ＿＿＿＿＿ For years I made excuses whenever friends suggested a day at the beach.
Last year my daughter started swimming lessons, and I spent every Saturday watching her from the side of the pool. (17) ＿＿＿＿＿ So I decided it was time to learn too.
The first lesson was terrifying. I held on to the side and refused to put my face in the water. (18) ＿＿＿＿＿ She explained that being afraid was normal and that we would go at my speed.
Slowly, things improved. After a month I could float on my back, and after three months I swam my first length. (19) ＿＿＿＿＿
Now I swim twice a week before work. (20) ＿＿＿＿＿ My daughter and I are even planning to swim in the sea together this summer.

四十歲學游泳
我小時候沒學過游泳。我家離海很遠，鎮上也沒有游泳池。等到長大成人，我已經不好意思開始學了。好多年來，朋友一提議去海邊，我就找藉口。
去年女兒開始上游泳課，我每個星期六都在池邊看她。全場只有我這個家長不會游泳，覺得很丟臉。於是我決定，自己也該學了。
第一堂課很可怕。我抓著池邊，不肯把臉放進水裡。幸好老師很有耐心。她說害怕很正常，我們會照我的速度來。
慢慢地，情況好轉了。一個月後我能仰漂，三個月後我游完了第一趟。我驕傲得差點哭出來。
現在我每週上班前游兩次，這成了我一週裡最快樂的時光。今年夏天，女兒和我甚至打算一起去海裡游泳。

items.text:
A year without new clothes
Last January, nineteen-year-old student Amy Chen made a decision that surprised her friends: for a whole year, she would not buy a single new piece of clothing. 'I used to go shopping every weekend,' she says. 'I had a wardrobe full of things I'd worn once or never. Then I read an article about how much water it takes to make one pair of jeans, and I felt terrible.'
The first few months were the hardest. 'Whenever I walked past a shop window, I wanted to go in,' Amy admits. 'So I stopped going into town on Saturdays and found other things to do, like volunteering at an animal shelter.' She also learned to repair her clothes. 'My grandmother taught me to sew. Before that, if a button came off, I'd just throw the shirt away.'
Amy did allow herself one exception: second-hand clothes. She and some friends started a monthly swap party, where everyone brings clothes they no longer wear and takes home something different. 'The first one had six people. Now we get over fifty, and the clothes nobody takes go to a charity shop.'
By December, Amy had saved more than a thousand pounds. But she says the money isn't the most important thing. 'I think more carefully now. Before I get anything, I ask myself if I'll still want it in a year.' Will she go back to her old habits? 'Never,' she laughs. 'Although I might buy some new running shoes — mine have a hole in them!'

tr.zh:
一整年不買新衣服
去年一月，十九歲的大學生陳艾咪做了一個讓朋友驚訝的決定：整整一年，她一件新衣服都不買。「我以前每個週末都去逛街，」她說，「衣櫃裡塞滿只穿過一次或從沒穿過的東西。後來我讀到一篇文章，講做一條牛仔褲要用多少水，我覺得很糟糕。」
頭幾個月最難熬。「每次經過櫥窗，我都想進去，」艾咪承認，「所以我星期六不再進城，改做別的事，像是去動物收容所當志工。」她也學會了補衣服。「奶奶教我縫紉。以前掉一顆扣子，我就直接把襯衫丟了。」
艾咪給自己留了一個例外：二手衣。她和幾個朋友每個月辦一次換衣派對，每個人帶自己不穿的衣服來，再帶走不一樣的。「第一次只有六個人，現在超過五十人，沒人要的衣服就送到慈善二手店。」
到了十二月，艾咪存了一千多英鎊。但她說錢不是最重要的。「我現在想得比較仔細。買任何東西之前，我會問自己一年後還會不會想要。」她會回到以前的習慣嗎？「絕對不會，」她笑著說，「不過我可能會買雙新的跑鞋，我的破了一個洞！」

Last spring I applied for a summer job at a busy outdoor activity centre. I was excited when they invited me for an interview, but also very nervous. (16) ＿＿＿＿＿

On the day, I arrived twenty minutes early and waited in reception. There were four other people there, all older than me. (18) ＿＿＿＿＿ But then I remembered my mum's advice: just be yourself.
The interview itself was not what I expected. Instead of sitting at a desk, the manager took me outside and asked me to help a group of children put up a tent. (19) ＿＿＿＿＿ Luckily, I had been camping many times with my family.
A week later, I got a phone call offering me the job. (20) ＿＿＿＿＿ It was the best summer of my life, and they've invited me back again this year.

When the drink arrived in Europe in the 1500s, people added sugar to make it (23) ＿＿＿＿＿ sweeter. For a long time, chocolate was so expensive that only rich people could (24) ＿＿＿＿＿ it. 巧克力的歷史
巧克力來自可可樹的種子，可可樹生長在炎熱的國家。幾千年前，中美洲的人用這些種子做成一種苦的飲料。這種飲料在十六世紀傳到歐洲後，人們加了糖讓它甜得多。很長一段時間，巧克力貴到只有有錢人買得起。固體巧克力棒直到十九世紀才被發明。現在，巧克力是全世界最受歡迎的甜食之一，有些人甚至說沒有它活不下去。

items.text:
Rescue on the mountain
Tom Baker, 34, is a teacher by day. But several times a month his phone rings in the middle of the night, and he has to leave his warm bed to help someone in trouble on the mountains near his home. Tom is one of forty volunteers in the local mountain rescue team.
'I grew up walking in these hills with my father,' he explains. 'When I was twenty, a friend of mine broke her leg up here, and the rescue team carried her down in the dark. I joined the next year because I wanted to give something back.'
Training takes at least a year. Volunteers learn first aid, how to use maps and radios, and how to carry a person safely down steep ground. 'The hardest part isn't the physical work,' Tom says. 'It's staying calm when someone is frightened or badly hurt.'
Most of the people the team helps are walkers who have got lost or been caught by bad weather. 'People often look at a sunny sky in the morning and don't take warm clothes,' says Tom. 'But up here, the weather can change in twenty minutes.' He advises walkers to always tell someone their plans and to carry a fully charged phone.
The team is not paid, and it depends on gifts from the public to buy equipment. Last year local people raised enough money for a new vehicle. 'It's a hard job,' Tom says, 'but when you bring someone home safely, there's no better feeling.'

tr.zh:
山上的救援
三十四歲的湯姆·貝克白天是老師。但每個月有好幾次，他的手機會在半夜響起，他得離開溫暖的床，去家附近的山上幫助遇到麻煩的人。湯姆是當地山難救援隊四十位志工之一。
「我從小跟爸爸在這些山裡健行，」他說，「我二十歲那年，一個朋友在山上摔斷了腿，救援隊在黑暗中把她抬下山。第二年我就加入了，因為我想回饋。」
訓練至少要一年。志工要學急救、看地圖和用無線電，還有怎麼把人安全地從陡坡抬下來。「最難的不是體力活，」湯姆說，「而是在對方害怕或傷得很重時保持冷靜。」
救援隊幫助的大多是迷路或碰上壞天氣的登山客。「很多人早上看天空晴朗，就不帶保暖衣物，」湯姆說，「可是在山上，天氣二十分鐘就能變。」他建議登山客一定要把計畫告訴別人，並帶著充飽電的手機。
救援隊沒有薪水，靠民眾捐款買裝備。去年當地居民募到了足夠買一台新車的錢。「這工作很辛苦，」湯姆說，「但把人平安帶回家，沒有比這更好的感覺了。」

As we got older, we started to want different things. Lucy loved sport, while I preferred art and music. (18) ＿＿＿＿＿ For the first time, we had different friends and spent our weekends apart.
At sixteen, Lucy decided to go to a sports college in another city. (19) ＿＿＿＿＿ I missed her terribly, but it also helped me discover who I was on my own.

Sleep and teenagers
Scientists say that teenagers need about nine hours of sleep a night, but most of them get much (21) ＿＿＿＿＿ than that. One reason is that teenagers' bodies naturally want to go to bed later. Another is that many teenagers use their phones in bed, and the light from the screen can (22) ＿＿＿＿＿ it harder to fall asleep. Not getting enough sleep can (23) ＿＿＿＿＿ concentration at school and even affect people's moods. Some schools have decided to (24) ＿＿＿＿＿ the school day later, and teachers say students are more awake in lessons. Experts suggest (25) ＿＿＿＿＿ phones out of the bedroom and going to bed at the same time every night, (26) ＿＿＿＿＿ at weekends.

tr.zh:
睡眠與青少年
科學家說，青少年每晚大約需要九小時的睡眠，但大多數人睡得遠比這少。原因之一是青少年的身體天生就想晚點睡。另一個原因是很多青少年在床上用手機，螢幕的光會讓人更難入睡。睡眠不足會降低上課時的專注力，甚至影響情緒。有些學校決定把上課時間往後延，老師說學生上課時比較清醒。專家建議不要把手機放在臥室，而且每晚同一時間上床，連週末也一樣。

Learning to cook at 40
I never learned to cook when I was young. My mum did all the cooking at home, and when I left home I lived on sandwiches and takeaways. Last year my doctor told me I needed to eat more healthily, so I finally decided to take a cookery course.
The first lesson was a disaster. I burned the rice and cut my finger. I almost didn't go back. But the teacher, Marco, told me that everyone makes mistakes at the start, and he was right. By the fourth week I could make a simple pasta dish without help.
What surprised me most was how much I enjoyed it. Cooking helps me relax after work, and I've started inviting friends for dinner — something I never did before. I've also saved a lot of money. My next plan is to learn to bake bread. — Daniel

tr.zh:
四十歲學做菜
我年輕時從沒學過做菜。家裡都是媽媽煮，離家後我靠三明治和外賣過活。去年醫生說我得吃得更健康，我終於決定去上烹飪課。
第一堂課糟透了：我把飯燒焦，還切到手指，差點不想再去。但老師馬可說，每個人一開始都會犯錯，他說得對。到第四週，我已經能自己做簡單的義大利麵。
最讓我驚訝的是我竟然這麼喜歡做菜。做菜讓我下班後放鬆，我也開始請朋友來吃晚餐，這是我以前從沒做過的。我還省了很多錢。下一步我打算學烤麵包。——丹尼爾

假期比較有挑戰。我們改搭火車旅行、住青年旅館。比開車慢，但去了很多原本不會去的地方。

The oldest library still in use is in Fez, Morocco. It was (21) ＿＿＿＿＿ in 859 by a woman called Fatima al-Fihri, who used the money her father had left her. For centuries, scholars travelled from all over the world to (22) ＿＿＿＿＿ its rare books. By the 20th century, however, the building was in (23) ＿＿＿＿＿ condition: water was coming through the roof and damaging the books. In 2012 an architect was asked to (24) ＿＿＿＿＿ it. She added modern air conditioning to protect the old books, but she was careful to (25) ＿＿＿＿＿ the original style. Today the library is open to the public, and visitors can (26) ＿＿＿＿＿ a look at some of its treasures.

tr.zh:
世界最古老的圖書館
至今仍在使用的最古老圖書館在摩洛哥的非斯，於八五九年由一位名叫法蒂瑪·菲赫里的女性用父親留給她的錢創立。幾個世紀以來，世界各地的學者遠道而來研讀珍貴的藏書。但到了二十世紀，建築狀況很差：屋頂漏水、損壞書籍。二〇一二年，一位建築師受託修復它。她加裝了現代空調保護古書，但小心保留了原本的風格。如今圖書館對大眾開放，參觀者可以看看部分珍藏。
